study_identification_part.si4_title: Structural brain abnormalities and aggressive behaviour in schizophrenia: Mega-analysis of data from 2095 patients and 2861 healthy controls via the ENIGMA consortium

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: This study aimed to investigate the neurobiological basis of the co-occurrence of positive symptoms, poor impulse control, and aggressive behavior in schizophrenia.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly states that the data came from the ENIGMA-Schizophrenia Working Group.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Data came from the Schizophrenia Working Group of the Enhancing Neuroimaging Genetics through Meta-Analysis (ENIGMA) consortium.

rci2_hc_n.reason: The paper provides the exact number of healthy controls.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: Twenty member sites contributed data to the current study. These sites were located in 13 different countries, with their samples totalling 2095 individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia ('patients') and 2861 unaffected general population controls ('healthy controls').

rci3_hc_age.supporting_text: Overall, the mean age of patients was 35 years (SD = 12) and that of healthy controls was also 35 years (SD = 13).

rci4_hc_sex.reason: The paper provides the number of male healthy controls, and the total number of healthy controls. The number of female participants was calculated by subtraction. The percentages were then calculated.
rci4_hc_sex.supporting_text: The proportion of men was higher in patients (n = 1391, 66%) than in healthy controls (n = 1404, 49%).

rci5_imaging_modality.reason: The paper mentions both T1-weighted and diffusion-weighted MRI.
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: All 20 sites acquired high-resolution (voxel size of ≤ 1 mm3 ) T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging scans...Nine sites also acquired diffusion-weighted images.

rci6_analysis_level.supporting_text: Based on the Desikan-Killiany atlas, structural measures were extracted for 34 cortical regions (cortical thickness [CT] and surface area [SA]) and 7 subcortical regions (volume) in each hemisphere...From these images, values of fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD) were extracted for 25 WM tracts in each hemisphere. This was done using tract-based spatial statistics.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The paper clearly states the software used for preprocessing.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: All 20 sites acquired high-resolution (voxel size of ≤ 1 mm3) T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging scans and processed these using FreeSurfer. ... This was done using tract-based spatial statistics in conjunction with the John Hopkins University atlas, implemented in FMRIB Software Library.

rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: For every IDP, we derived a normative model in the healthy controls using warped Bayesian linear regression with site, sex, age and -for local IDPs only -a global IDP as predictors.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: One-sample t-tests; Ordinal regression models; Generalised structural equation modelling for mediation analysis.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: This study provides evidence that the co-occurrence of positive symptoms, poor impulse control and aggressive behaviour in schizophrenia has a neurobiological basis, which may inform the development of therapeutic interventions.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Aggressive behaviour was significantly associated with reductions in total cortical volume (OR [99% CI] = 0.88 [0.78, 0.98], p = .003) and global white matter integrity (OR [99% CI] = 0.72 [0.59, 0.88], p = 3.50 × 10-5) and additional reductions in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex volume (OR [99% CI] = 0.85 [0.74, 0.97], p =.002), inferior parietal lobule volume (OR [99% CI] = 0.76 [0.66, 0.87], p = 2.20 × 10-7) and internal capsule integrity (OR [99% CI] = 0.76 [0.63, 0.92], p = 2.90 × 10-4). Except for inferior parietal lobule volume, these associations were largely mediated by increased severity of positive symptoms and reduced impulse control.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The study has a cross-sectional design, which precludes causal inference. Aggressive behavior was measured at a single point in time, which may have attenuated the effects. The measures of aggression were based on single items from broader clinical scales, not dedicated aggression instruments. Aggression and its potential mediators were assessed with the same instruments, raising the possibility of inter-item correlation effects. There was no information on comorbid antisocial personality disorder or psychopathy.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, its crosssectional design precludes causal inference...Second, aggressive behaviour was only measured at one point in time...Third, aggressive behaviour was measured with individual items of instruments designed for measuring symptoms and clinical features of schizophrenia...Fourth, aggressive behaviour and potential mediators were measured with the same instruments...Fifth, there was no information about comorbid ASPD or psychopathy.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: This is the first study in this field of research to measure structural brain abnormalities on an individual level. The findings may provide candidate neuroimaging markers for predicting treatment response and potential targets for neuromodulation therapies.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study is a mega-analysis of data from 20 international sites participating in the ENIGMA-Schizophrenia Working Group. The use of harmonized protocols for image processing and analysis is a key feature of this work.
